problem: The source is a paired vertical-line range plot (circle endpoints joined by stems with bracketed citation labels) but it is reconstructed as an unrelated scatter and the legend labels are garbled ("23, 4, 24", "his or").
suggested_fix: Detect vertical stem-with-endpoint range marks and keep paired endpoints as a single range series instead of emitting loose scatter points.

problem: The legend lists six series (a- and a+ variants) but only three are reconstructed; the a+ series sitting on the dashed zero line is dropped.
suggested_fix: Recover near-zero flat dashed series and avoid suppressing series that overlap the x-axis baseline.

problem: Two stray blue points appear near x=4.3 (y~0.005-0.006) that do not correspond to either of the two real curves.
suggested_fix: Reject isolated off-curve points that have no neighboring marks along the series trajectory.

problem: A spurious red fourth series with points at (-0.4,-448) and (0.4,-93) is added that does not exist among the three real line series.
suggested_fix: Suppress phantom series formed from axis/border artifacts and limit series count to detected legend entries.

problem: The dashed peak-pole offset series belongs to a secondary right axis (0 to -6) but is calibrated against the primary left axis, scrambling its values.
suggested_fix: Detect dual y-axes and calibrate the secondary-axis series against the right-axis ticks.

problem: Three legend entries (60/100/150 kHz) exist but the reconstruction labels only one series ("150 kHz (NKG)") despite plotting all three colors.
suggested_fix: Map each detected color cluster to its corresponding legend entry instead of collapsing to a single label.

problem: The source is a dense spaghetti band plot of many crossing curves but it is reconstructed as a meaningless multicolor scatter of line-crossing points.
suggested_fix: Treat dense overlapping line bands as continuous curves rather than emitting scatter points at intersections.

problem: Stray green and orange off-band points appear top-left and the categorical k-path x-axis is reconstructed as a spurious log scale (6.9e0 to 7.6e0).
suggested_fix: Drop off-curve outlier marks and treat non-numeric categorical axis ticks as ordinal positions instead of log values.
